yebhuyyasikā:
[Yebhuyya+ika+ā]  CL=7 The yebhuyyasikāvinayakamma is the vinaya rule for the majority decision in a deed or action. (A) The action or deed of causing a vote or ticket to be taken for the purpose of fostering a plentiful presence of dhammavādī individuals (those who speak about or uphold the Dhamma). (B) The action or deed of causing a vote or slip to be taken, ensures the accomplishment of creating a significant number of dhammavādī individuals. (C) The action or deed of resolving the vāvadādhikaraṇa (a dispute or contention) in a manner that depends on the support or consensus of many dhammavādī individuals. (The yebhuyyasikāsamatha is one of the seven methods of samatha (calming or settling), which serves to pacify the four types of adhikaraṇa (disputes or conflicts). See origin.
[Sa-āgama.]
